question: How much money does a farmer family get per year under PM-Kisan?
expected_answer: Rs 6,000 per year, paid directly into the bank account (DBT).

question: In how many instalments is the PM-Kisan benefit paid, and how much is each instalment?
expected_answer: Three instalments of Rs 2,000 each, one every 4 months.

question: Which periods of the year are the PM-Kisan instalments paid for?
expected_answer: April-July, August-November and December-March.

question: My grandfather owns farmland and gets a government pension of Rs 12,000 a month. Can he get PM-Kisan money?
expected_answer: No. Retired pensioners with a monthly pension of Rs 10,000 or more are excluded (except Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees).

question: Can a practising doctor who owns agricultural land get PM-Kisan benefits?
expected_answer: No. Professionals such as doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects registered with professional bodies and practising are excluded.

question: Is a farmer who paid income tax in the last assessment year eligible for PM-Kisan?
expected_answer: No. All persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year are excluded.

question: What is the cut-off date for deciding eligibility under PM-Kisan?
expected_answer: 01.02.2019 (1 February 2019); changes after that are not considered for the next 5 years, except transfer of land by succession due to death.

question: How does PM-Kisan define a farmer's family?
expected_answer: A family of husband, wife and minor children who own cultivable land as per the land records of the State/UT.

question: What is the age limit to join Atal Pension Yojana?
expected_answer: Between 18 and 40 years of age.

question: What monthly pension amounts can I choose under Atal Pension Yojana?
expected_answer: A guaranteed minimum monthly pension of Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 after age 60.

question: I paid income tax two years ago. Can I still join APY now?
expected_answer: No. From 1 October 2022, anyone who is or has been an income-tax payer cannot join APY.

question: What happens to the APY pension after the subscriber dies?
expected_answer: The spouse gets the same pension for life; after both the subscriber and spouse die, the pension wealth accumulated till age 60 is returned to the nominee.
key_facts: the spouse gets the same pension for life
after the spouse's death, the accumulated pension wealth goes to the nominee

question: How often can contributions be made to an APY account?
expected_answer: Monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, through auto-debit from a savings bank account.

question: What is the toll-free helpline number for Atal Pension Yojana?
expected_answer: 1800 1100 69 (PFRDA's APY help desk).

question: Is nomination compulsory when opening an APY account?
expected_answer: Yes. Providing nomination and spouse details is mandatory.

question: How much health cover does Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY give per family per year?
expected_answer: Up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
key_facts: up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year

question: My father is 72 and our family income is high. Can he still get Ayushman Bharat coverage?
expected_answer: Yes. Since the September 2024 expansion, all senior citizens aged 70 and above are covered regardless of income.

question: If a senior citizen above 70 is already part of a family covered by PM-JAY, do they get anything extra?
expected_answer: Yes, an additional top-up cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per year for themselves, not shared with family members under 70.
key_facts: up to Rs 5 lakh per year

question: Can a senior citizen who already has private health insurance benefit from PM-JAY?
expected_answer: Yes. Senior citizens covered by private health insurance or ESI are also eligible.

question: A 75-year-old retired central government employee is in CGHS. What are their options under PM-JAY?
expected_answer: They can either continue with their current scheme (CGHS) or opt for AB PM-JAY.

question: What type of treatment does PM-JAY cover?
expected_answer: Secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation.

question: In which states or UTs was PM-JAY not operational as of September 2024?
expected_answer: NCT of Delhi, West Bengal and Odisha (it was operational in 33 States/UTs).

question: How many digits does an ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) number have?
expected_answer: 14 digits.

question: Up to what age of the girl can a Sukanya Samriddhi account be opened?
expected_answer: Before the girl turns 10 years old.

question: What are the minimum and maximum amounts that can be deposited in a Sukanya Samriddhi account in a financial year?
expected_answer: Minimum Rs 250 and maximum Rs 1,50,000 per financial year.

question: For how many years can deposits be made into a Sukanya Samriddhi account?
expected_answer: Until 15 years from the date of opening the account.

question: When does a Sukanya Samriddhi account mature?
expected_answer: On completion of 21 years from the date of opening.

question: What interest rate does the Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme 2019 notification state?
expected_answer: 8.4 per cent per annum (as stated in the 2019 notification; rates are revised periodically).

question: My daughter is 17 and passed 10th standard. Can I withdraw money from her Sukanya account for her college fees, and how much?
expected_answer: Yes. Up to 50% of the balance at the end of the previous financial year can be withdrawn for education once she turns 18 or has passed 10th standard, whichever is earlier, with proof of admission or a fee slip.

question: How many Sukanya Samriddhi accounts can one family open?
expected_answer: For a maximum of two girl children, with exceptions for twins or triplets born in the first two orders of birth.

question: What is the penalty if the minimum deposit is not made in a Sukanya Samriddhi account?
expected_answer: The account is in default; it can be regularised within 15 years by paying Rs 50 penalty per year of default plus the minimum deposit for each defaulted year.

question: How much financial assistance is given to build a house under PMAY-G?
expected_answer: Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in North Eastern and hill states (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand) and the UTs of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
key_facts: Rs 1.30 lakh in North Eastern and hill states/UTs

question: What is the minimum size of a house built under PMAY-G?
expected_answer: 25 square metres, including a dedicated area for hygienic cooking.

question: Can PMAY-G beneficiaries get a loan, and on what terms?
expected_answer: Yes, a loan of up to Rs 70,000 at a 3% reduced interest rate; the maximum principal eligible for subsidy is Rs 2,00,000.

question: How much money can a PMAY-G beneficiary get for building a toilet?
expected_answer: Up to Rs 12,000 under Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin.

question: Our household earns Rs 18,000 a month and lives in a kutcha house. Are we eligible for PMAY-G?
expected_answer: No. Households with monthly income over Rs 15,000 (or paying income tax) are automatically excluded.

question: Does having a Kisan Credit Card exclude a household from PMAY-G?
expected_answer: Only if the Kisan Credit Card has a credit limit of Rs 50,000 or above.
key_facts: only if the credit limit is Rs 50,000 or above

question: What share of PMAY-G targets is reserved for SC/ST households?
expected_answer: A minimum of 60%.

question: When was PMAY-Gramin launched?
expected_answer: 20 November 2016.
